/LILIAN

Baltic Exchange Market Report 31 July 2026
Baltic Dry Index: 2732 (59)
Baltic Capesize Index: 4296 (129)
Baltic Panamax Index: 2087 (47)
Baltic Supramax Index: 1609 (-1)
Baltic Handysize Index: 887 (-3)
CAPESIZE
The market wrapped up the week on a firm footing, with sentiment continuing to improve despite activity naturally easing into the weekend. The BCI 5TC gained a further $1,165 to settle at $38,960, with C5 rising by $0.650 to $13.050 and C3 adding $0.380 to $34.160. In the Pacific, market conditions remained firm although the pace of trading tapered off as the week drew to a close. Two major miners were active on C5 alongside healthy operator demand, with owners maintaining a resolute stance throughout the session. Early bids opened around $12.50 following yesterday’s advance, but owners were seeking in excess of $13.00. One miner was reported to have fixed at $12.95, while another was understood to have covered, although details had yet to emerge, underlining the continued resistance from owners. The Atlantic maintained its positive trajectory, led by further gains in the South Atlantic and West Africa to China markets. Fixtures concluded yesterday on C3 in the very high $33s, around the $33.95 level, while today’s discussions centred on offers near $34.75 against bids around $33.75, reflecting the improving underlying sentiment despite limited fresh activity. The North Atlantic, meanwhile, experienced a quieter session with the overall tone remaining steady.
PANAMAX
Market conditions continued to strengthen today, with gains recorded across both the Atlantic and Pacific regions as confidence among owners remains on the rise. The market extended its upward trend, with the P5TC climbing by $417 to conclude the week at $18,780. The Atlantic basin once again led the advance, as brokers explained this has been supported by a limited supply of available vessels and steady cargo demand. Market sources highlighted that charterers who are seeking prompt coverage, especially for trans-Atlantic minerals runs, are facing increasing competition for open tonnage, resulting in firmer negotiations and higher concluded levels. Activity was particularly robust on fronthaul routes linked to the US East Coast, where a healthy flow of coal cargoes has kept vessel availability under pressure with sentiment continuing its positive tone. In the Pacific, market fundamentals also improved. Market sources have stated that grain demand from the North Pacific has provided the main source of support, while Australian coal volumes remains steady alongside Indonesia. The Kiran Africa (79,105 2011) open in Hong Kong 3/5 August was reported to have fixed in direct continuation to Lotus Ocean for a trip via Indonesia to Sout China with coal at $13,000.
SUPRAMAX
The week has ended on a relatively quiet note, with the 11TC average easing by $17 to close at $20,336. Despite the marginal decline, positive sentiment in the US Gulf provided support and helped underpin market sentiment. The Mediterranean market appears to have paused, with sources suggesting that any movement in rates remains largely positional. Both owners and charterers are said to be reassessing their positions and rate expectations ahead of next week. In the Pacific, while a reasonable volume of fixtures has been reported, market sentiment remains subdued. Industry sources continue to describe a softer market despite an improvement in the balance between available tonnage and cargo demand. The Seaglory (63,620 2026) open CJK fixed a trip redelivery West Africa at $21,000 with Chinaland, while the CHL Venus (56,023 2005) open Huanghua fixed to West Africa at $18,750 with Topsheen. Further activity in the Pacific saw the African Pheasant (63,507 2019) fixed from Cigading for a trip with coal redelivery Philippines at $18,000 with Lighthouse, while the Qinghe (52,450 2006) open Morowali was fixed for a nickel ore run at $17,000. The Star Norita (58,097 2012) open Son Duong 1/2 August fixed a trip to China at $12,500 and the Yangtze Dawn (56,700 2010) open Dhamra 2/4 August fixed iron ore fines to China at $12,000 to Austrans Bulk. Oldendorff were said to have fixed the Langlois Fujimaru (63,716 2025) coming open in Sohar for a minimum of 4 months at $22,000, although the exact period spread and delivery dates remain unknown.
HANDYSIZE
The Handysize market ended the week on a quiet note, with sentiment remaining generally soft across both basins and little fresh activity reported. European summer holidays continued to dampen trading interest in the Atlantic, while Asian markets also lacked momentum amid limited cargo enquiry and an ample supply of available tonnage. The subdued conditions were reflected in the index, with the HS7TC average declining by $58 to close at $15,969.

Across the Continent and Mediterranean, activity remained limited, with most participants focused on position management rather than fresh business. A Large Handy was reported on subjects for a trip from Garrucha to Rotterdam at low teens levels, although further details were not disclosed.

The South Atlantic and US Gulf remained subdued, with little visible fresh enquiry and no notable fixtures reported. Sentiment continued to appear weak as charterers showed little urgency and owners faced difficulty generating momentum.

In Asia, market conditions softened further as tonnage availability remained healthy across key loading areas while cargo volumes stayed limited. A 32,000-dwt was reported fixed from Dung Quat via Thailand range to South Philippines at $12,500. Elsewhere, market talk suggested a 42,000-dwt had achieved $19,000 for a deck cargo business, while an overage 32,000-dwt was reported fixed at $15,500, although voyage details remained unclear.

Market Fundamentals
China’s Manufacturing PMI

China’s manufacturing Purchasing Managers’ Index (PMI) fell 1.1 points from the prior month to a four-month low of 49.2 in July, standing below the 50-mark separating expansion from contraction, and the first month of contraction since March, National Bureau of Statistics data show.

Trading Commentary
Cape
The Cape FFA curve was well supported again as the physical market continues to tighten, pushing the index $1165 higher. The Aug and Sep were the biggest gainers today with 35900 and 37900 paid respectively, followed by the Oct contract with 38500 paid. The Sep v Oct spread narrowed and strengthened up to -800, together with the Aug v Q4 up to -1200. Significant volume goes through on the Q4 today

ai_analysis.summary: 干散货市场延续升势，BDI收涨59点至2732，Capesize和Panamax领涨，分别升129点和47点。Capesize 5TC突破38,960美元，C3和C5均创新高，Pacific和Atlantic双双向好。Panamax供应收紧推动大西洋市场走强，5TC涨至18,780美元。Supramax和Handysize小幅回落，市场整体情绪改善但基本面分化。

sections.title: Market Structure
sections.content: Capesize市场最为强劲，BCI 5TC大涨$1,165，Pacific主要矿商重返西澳，C3大西洋段站上$34。Panamax大西洋供应极度紧张，船东话语权增强，5TC周涨$417。Supramax微跌$17，Handysize跌$58，两者均受限于需求疲软。FFA市场Capesize Aug26突破35,750，Q1 27 Cal27录得125点涨幅，市场预期转暖。

sections.title: Dry Bulk Signals
sections.content: Capesize看多信号明确：C5站稳$13.00上方，C3突破$34，矿商采购活跃。Panamax大西洋供给侧收紧是核心驱动，跨大西洋航线竞争加剧。Supramax美国湾支撑市场但Pacific偏软。Handysize基本面最弱，亚洲吨位充裕压制运费。期货曲线近月升水结构支撑短期乐观情绪。

sections.title: Trading Focus
sections.content: 关注Capesize C5航线矿商议价能力，$13.00已成新支撑。Panamax大西洋供应紧张局面或持续至8月中旬，P1A_82突破$21,000。Supramax美国湾需求可持续性是关键变量。Handysize短期难以改善，亚洲吨位供需平衡仍需时间。远期曲线Q4 26至Q1 27价差收窄反映市场对明年上半年谨慎。

route_focus.view: Tubarao-Qingdao突破$34.160，大西洋段站上$33.95。巴西矿商活跃，南非至印度航线有$13.50出价，供给压力支撑高位。关注$34.50阻力位，短期内市场情绪持续向好。
Transatlantic RV大涨$1,064至$21,205，大西洋供给紧张是核心驱动。船东报价升至$22,000， charterers报价$19,000，价差扩大显示船东议价能力增强。短期供应难增，航线有望测试$22,000。
Skaw-Passero至Rio航线持平于$8,604，南大西洋需求疲软。Handysize整体偏弱，吨位供应充足压制运费。短期内无明显催化剂，预期维持底部震荡。
